correctness.rationale: For 1<p_n<=P and p_n->1, modular continuity at positive norms gives Phi(z/||z||)=1, and coordinate truncations tend in norm. For a norm-t far-tail y and fixed U>max(1,t), Phi(y/U) is trapped uniformly between (t/U)^(1+epsilon_N) and t/U, epsilon_N=sup_{n>N}(p_n-1)->0. Disjoint head/tail support gives the unique limiting L_x(t) by two-sided modular bracketing, independently of y. Every finite-codimensional Y meets every infinite-dimensional tail E_N nontrivially, giving the lower/upper universal quantifier bounds. Choosing Y=E_N gives reverse bounds via coordinate lattice monotonicity and a norm-small head approximation, so both pointwise moduli equal L_x(t)-1. For every U>1, sum |x_n|^p_n U^-p_n >=U^-P, with equality exactly on maximal-exponent coordinates; every fixed x has strict Phi(x/U)<U^-1, so L_x(t)<1+t, but L_{e_n}(t)->1+t. Thus delta_bar(t)=L_P(t)-1 achieved exactly on supported max P, rho_bar(t)=t not attained. For a sequence of far-out e_n, ||e_i-e_j||->2, so Kottman=2. Independent scalar root checks at t=.3,1 for head exponent 2, mixed head, and exponent 1.001 corroborate extremum orientation; infinite statements proven analytically.
